correctness_risks: Items must be hashable; Counter raises TypeError where list.count() worked.
Counter matches by hash + ==; list.count() by == only.

estimated_impact.note: qualitative heuristic; only the A/B benchmark measures the effect
estimated_impact.rationale: complexity change in the function that dominates the profile

expected_effect: Hypothesis: the quadratic rescans disappear (O(n) total), which should dominate for inputs with thousands of items.
memory_tradeoffs: One dict entry per distinct element.
observed_bottleneck: `count_duplicates` (workload.py:10) accounts for 99.3% of profiled time (cumulative 1.60 ms, exclusive 0.05 ms, 1 call(s)) in profile a82ee9b3-9c03-4b1f-b348-7a1aebed99d6 at size small [MEASURED]. Rule PP-COLL-001 flags linear list search/removal inside a loop at workload.py:13 [STATIC].

profiler_evidence.largest_non_workspace_functions_note: largest exclusive-time functions outside the workspace in the same profile; not attributed to a caller
profiler_evidence.note: cProfile instruments every call, so absolute times are inflated; percentages show where time goes, not how fast the code runs unprofiled.

proposed_optimization: Count every element in one pass with `collections.Counter(items)` before the loop and read the count from it.
suspected_root_cause: `items.count(x)` rescans the whole list on every call. Calling it for every element makes the function O(n^2).
title: Count elements once with collections.Counter
